# Figures (generated by figures/index.py; do not edit)

Run profile: **full** (5,000 Monte Carlo draws; formats png at 600 dpi). Every figure is drawn by the figures/ package from the data files listed (compute / draw separation).

## Main paper (paper_main/)

### Fig1_floor_area

**Fig1 Floor area: history and projection by demand band** — Floor area built per year by demand band: history as census-interval means (columns), the Reference projection annually from 2026 (2026 observed). Positive bands stacked up from zero, negative bands (the starting surplus and the overbuild absorbed, unconsented additions) down from zero. The black line is the floor area built (in scope), annual 1992-2050 (history from consents, projection from 2026); the grey caps on the history columns are the census-interval means. 2026 overbuild: observed 2026 building above need, fading from 2027; it is absorbed by 2035 together with the starting surplus (the 2024-25 building beyond the stock identity, carried into 2026).

- Files: `paper_main/Fig1_floor_area.png`
- Data: `data/baseline/bands_history.csv`, `data/baseline/bands_annual.csv`, `data/baseline/annual.csv`, `data/baseline/overbuild_2026.json`
- This run: Completions = 0.945 x consents lagged 17 months (median consent-to-completion time 1.27-1.53 yr; Greenaway-McGrevy & Jones 2023; Jones, Greenaway-McGrevy & Crow 2025; consistent with the Stats NZ Experimental building indicators). Households after the 2023 census = ERP / household-size path (Stats NZ DHE not used). Pipeline years 2026, 2027: building observed (consents to September 2026); the part above modelled need fades from 2028 (ρ = 0.43) and is absorbed by 2035. 2026 population: Stats NZ ERP nowcast. Six display bands (data/bands_display_map.csv); market balance = unexplained building + retirement villages (out of scope) + overbuild / pipeline excess + surplus absorbed (the starting surplus and the overbuild) + surplus kept vacant. Negative bands drawn down from zero: Market balance, Smaller households, Vacancy, Net replacement. Black line: floor area built (in scope), annual 1992-2050 (straight segments between year centres; history 1992-2025 from consents, projection from 2026); grey caps: census-interval means of the history columns (the mean of the annual values over each interval, checked). 2026-2050: 105.4 Mm².

### Fig2_reference_carbon

**Fig2 Embodied carbon of the Reference** — Annual embodied carbon of the Reference 2026-2050 by (a) demand type (the demand bands), (b) material and (c) life-cycle stage; (d) cumulative 2026-2050 as three attached columns of the same total by demand band, material and stage (negative demand bands solid below zero; the net total a black marker). Materials and stages are never negative.

- Files: `paper_main/Fig2_reference_carbon.png`

### Fig3_reference_boundaries

**Fig3 The Reference against the planetary boundaries** — (a) Annual carbon, Monte Carlo median with 50% and 90% bands, against the acquired-rights (AR) and ability-to-pay (AtP) boundaries and their zones; (b) cumulative carbon 2026-2050 with its Monte Carlo 90% interval (5th-95th percentile of the cumulative carbon) and 50% interval (25th-75th), the AR and AtP budgets, and the committed emissions after 2050: C1-C4 and B2/B4 after 2050, the latter a range (lower = 2050 factors held, upper = 2025 factors).

- Files: `paper_main/Fig3_reference_boundaries.png`
- Data: `data/aesa/annual.csv`, `data/montecarlo/annual_REF.csv`, `data/montecarlo/draws_REF.csv`, `data/baseline/projection.json`
- This run: Cumulative 2026-2050 25,503 kt (LoE AR 5.76, AtP 22.9); Monte Carlo 90% interval 21,197-30,569 kt (5th-95th percentile of the cumulative carbon of the draws), 50% interval 23,649-27,459 kt, median 25,521 kt (capped bars; the column is the deterministic Reference); committed after 2050 (drawn at the lower bound): C1-C4 5,702 kt (2025 factors) and B2/B4 after 2050 4,026 kt (2050 factors held; 4,960 kt with 2025 factors); Monte Carlo median 9,726 kt, 50% interval 9,069-10,456, 90% interval 8,160-11,519 kt. Committed range from the Monte Carlo floor-area uncertainty (population, household size, dwelling size, completion rate); repair and end-of-life factors held at their central values. Moderate / Ambitious Pathway and TL: deterministic runs. Lines are shape-preserving (PCHIP) interpolation through the annual values, not smoothed across the observed -> modelled join after 2027; bands: Monte Carlo 90% band pchip, Monte Carlo 50% band pchip.

### Fig4_pathways

**Fig4 The Pathways: the sequential waterfalls** — Sequential waterfalls of cumulative carbon 2026-2050 from the Reference, levers added in PAS 2080 order: (a) L1 ... L9 at Moderate -> Moderate Pathway; (b) at Ambitious -> Ambitious Pathway; (c) TL1 ... TL9 cumulative -> Theoretical Limit. Each step is one bar coloured by strategy with its net change; AR (solid) and AtP (dotted) budgets with their zones; order-free Shapley values in Fig6.

- Files: `paper_main/Fig4_pathways.png`
- Data: `data/pathways/annual.csv`, `data/pathways/waterfall.csv`, `data/pathways/waterfall_tl_from_reference.csv`
- This run: Cumulative LoE AR: REF 5.76, pathway-moderate 3.89, pathway-ambitious 2.59, TL 0.92. (a-c) Reference 25,503 kt -> Moderate Pathway 17,236 kt, Ambitious Pathway 11,459 kt, Theoretical Limit 4,079 kt; budgets AR 4,427 kt, AtP 1,113 kt. Steps in PAS 2080 order; each step is credited with what remains after the higher-priority measures; order-free Shapley values in Fig6. Net-positive steps: none.

### Fig5_solution_space

**Fig5 The solution space** — Cumulative level of exceedance of AR over uniform cuts of 2027-2050 floor area (x) and of carbon per m2 (y) (after Horup et al. 2025), with S1-S3 (Moderate filled, Ambitious hollow), the Moderate / Ambitious Pathway and the Theoretical Limit; analytic LoE AR contours and the exact AR line. Right: the cumulative LoE AR ruler (log) with the Reference, the Pathways, TL, AR = 1 and AtP; the same marker size per run in the plane, the ruler and the legend.

- Files: `paper_main/Fig5_solution_space.png`
- Data: `data/pathways/solution_space.csv`, `data/pathways/backcast.json`, `data/pathways/runs.csv`
- This run: LoE AR = [1,207 + 24,296 (1 - x)(1 - y)] / 4,427 kt; C_2026 = the 2026 cohort's emissions in the window; plane floor C_2026 / B_AR = 0.273 (the lowest LoE AR at x or y = 100%); AtP = B_AtP / B_AR = 0.251 lies below the floor, so the AtP contour is outside the plotted square (y = 100.4% at x = 0). Axes -5% to 90%.

### Fig6_shapley_levers

**Fig6 What each lever removes** — Shapley values within each combined game (Reference -> Moderate Pathway, -> Ambitious Pathway, -> TL; exact, 512 subsets) on cumulative carbon 2026-2050: rows grouped by PAS 2080 strategy (S1 Avoid, S2 Switch, S3 Improve) in the lever order and coloured by strategy; filled bar Moderate, hollow bar Ambitious, large dot TL. The TL dots are Shapley values within the TL game (all nine levers at their limit), so they include each lever's interactions at the limit; L5 (occupancy density) interacts with L4 (extra space): both act on the floor area per dwelling.

- Files: `paper_main/Fig6_shapley_levers.png`
- Data: `data/pathways/shapley.csv`
- This run: (a) Standalone: each lever alone vs the Reference (not additive). (b) Shapley shares within each combined game (Reference -> Moderate Pathway, -> Ambitious Pathway, -> TL; 512 subsets per game); the TL shares include interactions at the limit (L5 with L4). Game totals (= Reference - Pathway / TL): moderate 8,267 kt, ambitious 14,044 kt, tl 21,424 kt.

### Fig7_uncertainty

**Fig7 Uncertainty** — (a) One-at-a-time ranges of the Reference cumulative LoE AR 2026-2050, each input at its low and high end per its definition (population rows move the budgets with the path; AR base-window rows move the AR budget only); rows are shown from the completion-rate range up, without the completion-rate and no-2026-data rows (both in Extended Data Fig. 4; the rows with a smaller range are named, with their ranges, in the note); not additive, not a joint interval. (b) The Reference, the Moderate and Ambitious Pathways and the Theoretical Limit: cumulative LoE AR against the 2050 New Zealand population on the same paired Monte Carlo draws, P(LoE AR <= 1) of each with its Wilson 95% interval, LoE = 1, and the population at which the Theoretical Limit has P(LoE AR <= 1) = 50% (Firth logistic; bootstrap 95% CI).

- Files: `paper_main/Fig7_uncertainty.png`
- Data: `data/sensitivity/tornado.csv`, `data/sensitivity/planetary_boundary.csv`, `data/pathways/montecarlo_draws.csv`, `data/pathways/annual.csv`, `data/pathways/montecarlo_conditional_tl.json`, `data/baseline/scenarios.json`, `data/aesa/results.json`
- This run: (b) Below about 6.2 M (every draw below 6.03 M; 434 draws in all) the Theoretical Limit LoE AR flattens at about 0.6 (median 0.61, range 0.58–0.65): the dwellings released by TL1 (household merging) and TL2 (zero vacancy) plus the starting surplus cover all positive need after the pipeline, so TL builds no new dwellings after 2027 and its carbon is that of the observed 2026–27 pipeline (9.48 Mm²), which does not fall with population (correlation −0.02 over these draws; a year with negative need builds nothing and nothing is demolished). (a) Reference LoE AR 5.761; population rows move the budgets with the path; the AR base-window row moves the AR budget only; one-at-a-time ranges are not additive. Rows in Extended Data Fig. 4 only: Completion rate (0.93–0.96); No 2026 data (consents to Dec 2025). The carbon-factor rows (Carbon factors (jackknife), LoE AR 5.734–5.771 against carbon −3.4% / +3.2%) are not shown: their LoE range falls below the row filter (the range of the completion-rate row) because the AR base co-varies with the factors, so the AR budget moves with the carbon. (b) P(TL within AR) = 0.640 (Wilson 0.627-0.653; n = 5,000); P(LoE AR <= 1) on the same paired draws: Reference 0.0000 (Wilson 0.0000-0.0008), Moderate Pathway 0.0000 (Wilson 0.0000-0.0008), Ambitious Pathway 0.0000 (Wilson 0.0000-0.0008), Theoretical Limit 0.6400 (Wilson 0.6266-0.6532); threshold 6.715 M (95% CI 6.713-6.718 M; Firth penalised likelihood (MLE does not exist), 2000 resamples).

### ED4_one_at_a_time

**ED4 One at a time: cumulative embodied carbon 2026-2050 of the Reference** — One-at-a-time ranges of the Reference cumulative embodied carbon 2026-2050, grouped by category; each input at its low (pale blue) and high (dark blue) end, a single alternative case grey, intermediate cases as ticks; not additive, not a joint interval. Not shown (kept in the data file): the overbuild gap against the 2026 requirement, no census under-construction correction, the maintenance event timing L / n, and the rows that compare with superseded settings (their changes are in the note). What each row changes compared with the Reference (numbered as the row labels): [1] Stats NZ Medium B household projection (living-arrangement propensities change, modelled on the 2001–2023 censuses) instead of Medium A (propensities held at 2023): what if B happens anyway (the same path is L1 Ambitious, what if policy delivers it). [2] Stats NZ 2024-base stochastic projection, 5th / 95th percentile path instead of the median, with the household size of the Stats NZ Low / High A household projection (the same percentiles). [3] household size continues linearly from 2023 at the 2018–2023 census-interval pace instead of the Stats NZ household-size path rebased on 2023. [4] a zero slope imposed at 2048 and household size held constant after it instead of the 2043–2048 secant slope at 2048, continued linearly in 2049–2050. [5] the shape-preserving (PCHIP) end derivative at 2048, continued linearly, instead of the 2043–2048 secant slope at 2048, continued linearly in 2049–2050. [6] new-dwelling size held at its 2016–2025 mean per typology instead of the 2023–2025 mean. [8] the 2026 overbuild (building above need in 2026–2027 and its continuation, fading at ρ = 0.43) replaces existing dwellings instead of adding to the stock: no surplus, so no absorption payback and no soil carbon loss on it. [9] 0.93 / 0.96 of consented dwellings completed instead of 0.945. [10] a starting surplus of 6,812 dwellings (only the excess above the mean + 2 SD) instead of 18,966. [11] the mean of the 1986–2023 censuses on one definition instead of the 2023 census value (5.39%). [12] the starting surplus and the 2026 overbuild absorbed by 2030 / 2045 instead of 2035. ### ED5_boundary_sensitivity

**ED5 Boundary definitions and allocation: cumulative LoE of AR and of AtP** — One-at-a-time ranges of the Reference cumulative level of exceedance 2026-2050 of (a) acquired rights (AR) and (b) ability to pay (AtP): boundary definitions (carrying capacity, global impact, AR base window), allocation, population and replacement. Not shown (kept in the data file): α = 1 (Hjalsted et al. SI tables) and the raw Stats NZ 2024-base median population. What each row changes compared with the Reference (numbered as the row labels): [1] 1 W/m² planetary boundary (Bjørn & Hauschild 2015), safe operating space 3.61 × 10¹² kg CO₂e per year, instead of the 2 °C carrying capacity (Bjørn & Hauschild 2015), 6.81 × 10¹² (the same global impact); both budgets move. [2] global impact (I_glob) from the EF 3.1 normalisation factor (Andreasi Bassi et al. 2023, Table 10; 7.55 × 10³ kg CO₂e per person, 2010) instead of 5.58 × 10¹³ (Bjørn & Hauschild 2015; equal to the EF 3.0 factor, 8.10 × 10³ per person). The 6.7% difference is mainly the lower characterisation factor of methane in EF 3.1. Acquired rights only. [3] mean sector emissions over 5 / 20 / 34 years (2021–2025, 2006–2025, 1992–2025) instead of 10 years (2016–2025); AR only. [4] GDP per capita in current US$ instead of GDP per capita at purchasing-power parity, constant 2021 international $ (World Bank WDI); AtP only. [5] FCE share of GDP in the sector share: the ratio of the summed FCE to the summed GDP of the 40 quarters 2016–2025 instead of the mean of the 40 quarterly FCE/GDP ratios 2016–2025; AtP only. [6] Stats NZ 2024-base 5th / 95th percentile path instead of the median; carbon and both budgets move together. [7] UN WPP 2024 median for New Zealand instead of the model's population path (the Stats NZ 2024-base median from the observed 2025 level, with the observed 2026 growth); budgets only. [8] as in Extended Data Fig. 4 (carbon only; the budgets are unchanged). [9] as in Extended Data Fig. 4 (carbon only).

SI tables); the raw Stats NZ 2024-base median population (in the data file). Row notes: [1] 1 W/m² planetary boundary (Bjørn & Hauschild 2015), safe operating space 3.61 × 10¹² kg CO₂e per year, instead of the 2 °C carrying capacity (Bjørn & Hauschild 2015), 6.81 × 10¹² (the same global impact); both budgets move. [2] global impact (I_glob) from the EF 3.1 normalisation factor (Andreasi Bassi et al. 2023, Table 10; 7.55 × 10³ kg CO₂e per person, 2010) instead of 5.58 × 10¹³ (Bjørn & Hauschild 2015; equal to the EF 3.0 factor, 8.10 × 10³ per person). ### ED7_sobol

**ED7 Sobol indices of the Reference: embodied carbon and floor area 2026-2050**

- Files: `paper_extended/ED7_sobol.png`
- Data: `data/montecarlo/sobol_REF.csv`
- This run: Reference, cumulative 2026–2050; Saltelli / Jansen estimators (scipy.stats.sobol_indices); 95% intervals by bootstrap of the Sobol samples; full profile only. Population and household size are one grouped input: both are drawn from one standard-normal score z (perfectly dependent), so their indices are grouped Sobol indices (Jacques, Lavergne & Devictor 2006).

## Supplementary figures (supplementary/)

### SF1_households

**SF1 Households: the published and census-benchmarked series, and household size against population growth**

- Files: `supplementary/calibration/SF1_households.png`
- Data: `data/figure_source/D02_households.json`, `data/figure_source/D04_household_formation.json`
- This run: a: projection from the 2023 census point; 2019–23 Stats NZ estimates scaled to the 2023 census (×0.824); 2024–2025: households = population / household size (model), on the projection line. The band: the 5th / 95th population percentile paths with the Stats NZ Low A / High A household size (households computed per path). b: between censuses households are consent-derived, so the relationship is partly mechanical (housing supply meets migration); 2024-25 are the model household-size path (ERP / S), not observations.

### SF2_stock_vacancy

**SF2 Vacancy, dwellings per year by component and the vacancy definition**

- Files: `supplementary/calibration/SF2_stock_vacancy.png`
- Data: `data/figure_source/D05_stock_and_vacancy.json`, `data/figure_source/D06_vacancy_definition.json`, `data/baseline/scenarios.json`, `data/baseline/projection.json`
- This run: a: The vacancy-rate parameter is held at its published 2023 census value (5.39%; on the consistent definition 2023 is the series maximum, 5.38%, minimum 4.01% in 1996); the starting surplus and the 2026 overbuild raise implied stock vacancy temporarily and are absorbed by 2035, so implied vacancy returns to the parameter (5.39% in 2050). c: the unconsented additions each vacancy definition requires to close the stock identity (BRANZ demolition rate); counting residents-away dwellings as vacant requires implausibly many. b: History: one column per census interval (interval means; vacancy on one definition, the pooled 2018/2023 empty share, 49.2% of unoccupied dwellings); between censuses annual detail is not identified. The 2024–2025 column (marked †): households are population / household size (model), not census-benchmarked; its market balance (9,020 dwellings a year) is the F1 residual, carried into 2026 as the starting surplus (18,966 dwellings). Pipeline years 2026, 2027: annual columns; projection from 2028: annual stacked areas. In the pipeline years the line is the sum of the components (the stock-identity count: observed building less the modelled retirement-village share); the in-scope floor area divided by the dwelling size held at its 2023–2025 mean gives 2026: 30,045 (−51); 2027: 35,540 (−801) (the pipeline floor area is observed, the dwelling size held). History: net replacement is census-measured, the rate of the census dwelling-count identity of each interval (SF3; under-construction corrected) x the previous year's stock, the quantity the model uses (2024–2025: the latest rate carried). Top row: the market balance per census interval (thousand dwellings per year). Market balance: building above (+) or below (−) what household growth, vacancy and net replacement require. History: the residual of the census stock identity (includes measurement error). 2024–25: carried into 2026 as starting surplus (18,966 vacant dwellings: the residual above the census-interval mean x 2 years). 2026–27: the observed pipeline above need. From 2028: the surplus absorbed by 2035. The same band as Fig1's market balance (checked in 32 intervals and years: the same sign everywhere, and Fig1 = the dwellings x the in-scope floor area per dwelling after the pipeline; Fig1 also counts the retirement villages, drawn here on their own). Projection: net replacement, retirement villages (negative) and the market balance. Net replacement = demolition − unconsented additions (+ the recent surge in the Reference); the census measures only the net. The projection's split (demolition at the BRANZ rate, 0.135%/yr; the calibrated residual as unconsented additions, −0.076%/yr; the surge) is not identified from data and is not drawn. Positive parts are stacked up from zero and negative parts down from zero, all solid (no outlines, hatching or fades); up + down = the net of every column and year (checked). The line is the annual dwellings built (in scope), straight between annual values; the grey caps are its census-interval means (equal to the column nets, checked). The row at the top: the market balance of each census interval (thousand dwellings per year).

### SF6_hindcast

**SF6 Rolling-origin hindcast of dwellings built and the 2027 out-of-sample check**

- Files: `supplementary/validation/SF6_hindcast.png`
- Data: `data/figure_source/D14_hindcast.json`, `data/baseline/validation.json`
- This run: Rolling-origin hindcast of dwellings built (cumulative), each origin projected with the information available then; errors at the end of each window, vacancy on the consistent definition. The four replacement variants use only the census intervals ending at or before the origin: Low the long-run dwelling-count rate, Reference the last intercensal rate fading to it (10-year half-life), High the last rate held, Very High the weighted linear trend of the interval rates (3, 4 and 5 intervals at the 2006, 2013 and 2018 origins). d: building of the first year the run without 2026 data models, observed in the pipeline (consents lagged), against that run.

### SF7_completion_lag

**SF7 Annual floor area by demand group: 17-month and like-for-like zero completion lag**

- Files: `supplementary/validation/SF7_completion_lag.png`
- Data: `data/diagnostics/lag_comparison_annual.csv`, `data/diagnostics/lag_comparison_summary.json`
- This run: All runs use identical source files and demographic paths. The like-for-like zero-lag run holds the forward net replacement at the 17-month calibration (2018-2023 rate 0.173%/yr), so it differs from the 17-month run only in the timing of building. The recalibrated zero-lag run (grey, context) re-estimates net replacement from the census counts with zero-lag timing (0.301%/yr with the census under-construction correction); its higher net replacement in panel c is that recalibration, not the timing of building. Cumulative net replacement 2026-2050: 9.02 Mm² (zero lag, held), 9.29 Mm² (17 months), 15.24 Mm² (zero lag, recalibrated). Zero lag treats a rolling 12-month consent estimate as the 2026 build proxy; the 17-month run uses complete observed consent cohorts for 2026 and 2027.

### SF13_conditional_tl

**SF13 When does TL stay within AR? By population quintile and the population threshold**

- Files: `supplementary/montecarlo/SF13_conditional_tl.png`

- This run: P(within AR) = 0.640 (Wilson 0.627-0.653); (b) threshold 6.72 M (95% CI 6.71-6.72 M; Firth penalised likelihood (MLE does not exist), 2000 resamples). TL1 holds household size at 2.79 (1991, the highest observed) regardless of age structure: with the 2050 population this requires about 11.7% fewer households per person than in 2023 at every age. With an age-standardised TL1 (the lower of the 2023 and Stats NZ Medium B living-arrangement rates by age group; never below L1 Ambitious, which binds from 2040) TL is 5,946 kt, LoE AR 1.34, P(LoE AR ≤ 1) = 0.1% over the draws (the sensitivity row TL-TL1-age-standardised).
